node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 uses "[the fact filing_date] is greater than or equal to [date value 2026-02-02]", potentially triggering resubmission during the blackout before 9:00am. The source's calendar-date wording and operational-launch wording support competing temporal interpretations that should remain explicit.

The launch-based candidates select 9:00am as the boundary. This has support in da12aecad4e68.u13.2131, but does not independently resolve the relationship between "With effect from 2 February 2026" and "following its implementation", or establish a timezone.

Footnote 3 says "Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission." Availability is not established as sufficient; the stated assumption does not resolve that interpretive gap.
node.91c869d719c8872846f5adba delegates certificate compliance to "ecert_requirement_satisfied". This avoids equating possession with compliance but leaves the required mechanics externally assessed.

The compliance candidates assess the selected channel, method and e-Cert control, not all circular obligations. XML format selection cannot establish compliance with the separately required XML schema.

Direct urgent contact during the blackout is expressly contemplated by da12aecad4e68.u12.1941. Neither that contact nor automatic migration alone establishes an original submission event triggering resubmission.

A report-history trigger records whether a qualifying event existed, not whether a resubmission duty remains outstanding after later performance. Its externally supplied existence predicate must preserve report identity and sufficient history for a false result.
